title: Your First Program
lessonSummary: Done. print() is fundamental – you'll see it in every Python script.

tasks.instruction: Print "Hello World".
Print your name in a greeting, e.g. "Hi, I'm Alex!".
Print three different lines using three print() calls. Each line should contain "Line".

title: Variables
lessonSummary: Good. Variables are the basic building block of every program.

tasks.instruction: Store "Python" in a variable and print it.
Store the number 2024 in a variable and print it.
Create two variables first_name and last_name and print them together, e.g. "Max Mustermann".

title: Numbers and Arithmetic
lessonSummary: Good. Python as a calculator – you'll need this constantly.

tasks.instruction: Calculate the average of [80, 92, 75, 88] – add all values and divide by 4.
Calculate 2 to the power of 10 (2 ** 10) and print the result.
Calculate the remainder of 17 divided by 5 using the % operator.

title: Data Types
lessonSummary: Good. Types are implicit in Python – but you should always know what you're working with.

tasks.instruction: Print the type of 3.14.
Convert the string "42" to a number and print its type.
What does type(True) return? Print it.

title: Formatting Strings (f-Strings)
lessonSummary: Good. f-Strings are standard in modern Python code.

tasks.instruction: Create variables name and age and print a sentence: "Alex is 17 years old."
Create a variable score = 850 and print: "Highscore: 850 points."
Calculate 15% of 80 directly in the f-String and print: "15% of 80 = 12.0"

title: Conditions with if
lessonSummary: Good. Conditions control program flow – the core principle behind almost every logic.

tasks.instruction: Print "Adult" if a variable age is at least 18, otherwise print "Minor".
Check with if/elif/else: Under 13 → "Child", 13-17 → "Teenager", 18+ → "Adult".
Check if a number is even (% 2 == 0). Print "even" or "odd".

title: Loops with for
lessonSummary: Good. Loops are the workhorse for repetition in real programs.

tasks.instruction: Iterate over a list ["Python", "Java", "JavaScript"] and print each language.
Print all even numbers from 0 to 10 (range with step 2).
Print the numbers 1-5 in reverse (range with negative step).

title: Lists
lessonSummary: Good. Lists are one of the most frequently used data structures in Python.

tasks.instruction: Create a list numbers = [5, 3, 8, 1, 9] and print its length.
Sort the list numbers and print the first element (smallest number).
Add the number 4 to the list and print the new length.

title: Functions
lessonSummary: Good. Functions are the most important tool for structured, maintainable code.

tasks.instruction: Define square(n) that calculates n² and prints it with print(). Call it with 7.
Define celsius_to_fahrenheit(c) – formula: (c * 9/5) + 32. Call it with 0.
Define maximum(a, b) that prints the larger of the two numbers. Test with 15 and 23.

title: Dictionaries
lessonSummary: Good. Dictionaries are everywhere in Python – JSON, APIs, configs, all dictionaries.

tasks.instruction: Create a dictionary with "language": "Python" and "version": 3. Print the value of "language".
Add a new key "popular" with value True to the dictionary and print True.
Iterate over all key-value pairs using .items() and print them.

title: Exercise: Putting It All Together
lessonSummary: Done. You've mastered the Python basics. Time for the 12-week course!

tasks.instruction: Create a list numbers = [3, 7, 2, 9, 1] and print each number doubled.
Define total(numbers) that prints the sum with print(). Call it with [10, 20, 30, 40].
Create a dictionary {"Alice": 25, "Bob": 30, "Charlie": 20} and print all names using a for loop.
